title: A flaky or absent connection dumps a fully set-up user into the "A little about you" onboarding form
userImpact: Open the app on a subway, a plane, hotel wifi, or during a Supabase hiccup and you are not shown your chat, not shown an error, and not shown sign-in — you are shown the new-account name/date-of-birth form. It reads as "the app forgot me and deleted everything." Filling it in fails too. There is no offline mode and no retry screen. This will happen to a meaningful fraction of strangers in week one.
evidence: mobile/lib/core/app/session_provider.dart:259-263 — `catch (e) { state = state.copyWith(loading: false, error: e.toString()); }`. The comment above it claims "let the router redirect to sign-in so the user is never stuck forever", but `copyWith` deliberately preserves `session` (session_provider.dart:47-56), so `isAuthenticated` stays true. Router then evaluates mobile/lib/core/app/router.dart:107-113: `needsProfile = session.profile == null` → true → `return '/welcome'`. Confirmed dead end for the error text: `SessionState.error` is declared at session_provider.dart:35, written at :262, and grep for a reader across all 238 dart files returns zero hits — nothing in the app ever displays it.
fix: Distinguish "profile not fetched" from "user has no profile". Keep the last good profile in secure storage and hydrate from it on launch; when the fetch throws, render a "Can't reach Miles right now — Retry" screen (read `SessionState.error`, which is already populated) instead of falling through the onboarding funnel. Only route to /welcome when the server actually answered with no profile row.
effort: M — one guard in the router plus a persisted profile snapshot and an error screen

title: Sign-up is a one-shot email with no resend, on a mailer capped at 2 messages per hour for the whole project
userImpact: If the confirmation mail is slow, filtered to spam, or throttled, the stranger is stuck permanently. "Sign in" answers "Please confirm your email first"; the only other button is "Send a reset link", which they have no reason to press. On launch day, user #3 onward in any given hour simply never receives an email and the app looks broken to everyone but the first two.
evidence: No resend path exists: `grep -rn "resend\|resendOtp\|OtpType.signup" lib` returns zero hits across 238 files. The post-submit screen offers only two actions — mobile/lib/features/auth/sign_up_page.dart:170-178 ("Sign in" / "Send a reset link"). The failure message for an unconfirmed sign-in is mobile/lib/features/auth/auth_errors.dart:57-59. The quota is documented in this repo: docs/architecture/research/supabase.md:151 — "built-in SMTP 2 emails/hour project-wide" — and docs/guides/BRAIN.md:2381 records it as still unresolved ("No `[auth.email.smtp]` block in config.toml, so the shared built-in sender is in use; the actual cap is dashboard-side"). supabase/config.toml:53-56 has `enable_confirmations = true` and no smtp block. Live prod check (`select count(*) from auth.users` on sopictusdonlvuezmfep) returns **3 users, 1 couple** — this path has never been exercised beyond the owner's own pair. UNVERIFIED: whether custom SMTP is configured dashboard-side; settled by Supabase Dashboard → Project Settings → Authentication → SMTP Settings.
fix: Two things, both required. (1) Configure a real SMTP provider (Resend/Postmark/SES) on the prod project before any store listing goes live — the built-in sender is explicitly development-only. (2) Add a "Resend confirmation email" button to the sign_up_page sent-state with a 60s throttle (the same shape already written for password reset at sign_in_page.dart:92-99), calling `auth.resend(type: OtpType.signup, email: ...)`.
effort: S for the button; S for SMTP config, but it must not be skipped

title: Gender is a mandatory binary choice with no skip, and the router will not let you past it
userImpact: After pairing, every route in the app redirects to a screen offering exactly two buttons: "I'm male" and "I'm female". There is no third option, no "prefer not to say", no skip. A non-binary user, or anyone who simply does not want to declare it to a couples app, cannot use the product at all — they are trapped in a redirect loop with no exit (the sign-out escape only appears after a *save failure*). This is a guaranteed one-star review and a support thread.
evidence: mobile/lib/core/app/router.dart:119-123 — `final needsRole = ... !session.profile!.genderSet; if (needsRole) return path == '/role-setup' ? null : '/role-setup';`. The screen offers two cards only: mobile/lib/features/auth/role_setup_screen.dart:84-99. The sign-out escape is gated on `_failed` (role_setup_screen.dart:24, :58-71), so it is invisible on the normal path.
fix: Add a third, non-blocking option ("Prefer not to say" / "Skip") that sets `gender_set = true` with a null gender, and make the cycle feature check `isFemale` rather than assuming one of two values. Keep the sign-out affordance visible unconditionally.

title: The Play build tears the whole app down and rebuilds it every time you switch away — for users who never chose a disguise
userImpact: A stranger opens WhatsApp to paste the invite code, comes back, and the app has restarted: a blank frame, then every screen's state gone. Chat re-downloads from the network behind a spinner instead of appearing instantly. Scroll position, half-composed states, in-progress screens — all lost, every single time, on a build where the user has no cover and gets nothing in return for the cost.
evidence: The play flavour sets `DISGUISE_ENABLED` true — mobile/android/app/build.gradle.kts:152. So `DisguiseService.enabled` is true and `MilesApp.raiseCover()` (mobile/lib/main.dart:160-162) fires on every `paused`/`hidden`/`detached` and settled `inactive` (main.dart:305-361), swapping the entire `MaterialApp.router` for `DisguiseCoverHost` (main.dart:775-790). The host renders `SizedBox.shrink()` (mobile/lib/features/disguise/disguise_cover_host.dart:81) until an async platform-channel `reconcile()` resolves (disguise_cover_host.dart:42-60, disguise_service.dart:177-199). The codebase documents the consequence itself: "the cover REPLACES the router subtree, so this State is destroyed every single time" (mobile/lib/features/auth/sign_in_page.dart:31-35) and "leaving the app drops the cover over everything and destroys this screen" (mobile/lib/features/auth/couple_page.dart:47-51). Chat then shows `_loading ? CircularProgressIndicator()` (mobile/lib/features/chat/chat_screen.dart:1542) with no local store to fall back on — `grep drift|sqflite|hive|isar` in pubspec.yaml returns nothing.
fix: Gate the teardown on whether a cover is actually in use, not on the build flag: `raiseCover()` should no-op when the active identity is `DisguiseCover.none`. Users who pick a cover in Settings keep today's behaviour; everyone else keeps their app alive across an app switch.
effort: S for the guard; M if you also want a persisted message cache

title: The first screen a stranger ever sees is a sign-in form saying "Welcome back"
userImpact: Install from Play, open, and the app demands an email and password cold. There is no explanation of what Miles is, no screenshots, no value proposition, no "what happens next", and the default action is Sign in rather than Create account. The subtitle references a "countdown" the user has never heard of. A meaningful share of installs bounce right here without ever creating an account.
evidence: mobile/lib/core/app/router.dart:364-367 — `'/'` redirects to `'/signin'`; router.dart:85-87 — an unauthenticated user can only reach `/signin` or `/signup`. mobile/lib/features/auth/sign_in_page.dart:133-134 — `title: 'Welcome back', subtitle: 'Your countdown is waiting.'`. `find lib -name '*onboard*' -o -name '*welcome*' -o -name '*intro*'` returns only `auth/welcome_page.dart` (a post-signup profile form) and `intro/intro_splash_screen.dart` (a 900ms wordmark fade used only behind the disguise gate, cover_gate.dart:123). No carousel, no value screen, nothing.
fix: Add a 3-card intro before /signin: what Miles is, that it is for exactly two people, and that one of you invites the other. Make "Create account" the primary button and "I already have an account" secondary. Land on this screen at `/` instead of redirecting to /signin.

title: There is no way to send an invite — only "Copy code" and a link that no messaging app can open
userImpact: The only two-person app mechanic in the product has no share sheet. The user must copy a code, leave the app (which restarts it, see above), find their partner's chat, paste, and then talk their partner through installing an app they have never heard of. The "Copy link" button is worse than useless: it produces `tethered://join?code=XXXXXXXX`, which WhatsApp/SMS/Instagram render as dead plain text, and which does nothing at all on a phone that has not installed Miles yet. There is no Play Store fallback, so an invite can never reach the person it is for.
evidence: `grep share_plus pubspec.yaml` and `grep -rn "Share\.\|shareXFiles" lib` both return zero — no share sheet exists anywhere in the app. The invite actions are clipboard-only: mobile/lib/features/auth/couple_page.dart:392-415 ("Copy code" / "Copy link") and mobile/lib/features/home/home_screen.dart:582-591 ("Copy code" only). The link format is mobile/lib/features/auth/couple_page.dart:19 — `'tethered://join?code=$code'`. mobile/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:156-161 declares only the `tethered` scheme; `grep -n "https://\|autoVerify" AndroidManifest.xml` returns nothing — there is no https App Link.
fix: Add `share_plus` and a "Invite your partner" button that opens the system share sheet with a short https URL (e.g. `https://miles-legal.vercel.app/join?code=XXXX` on the domain you already own and which already returns 200). Serve a page there that deep-links into the app if installed and offers the Play listing if not, and add an `autoVerify` App Link intent-filter for that host.

title: Notifications are requested cold with no reason, and a refusal is silent and permanent
userImpact: Seconds after entering the app, Android's notification dialog appears with no explanation of why. Refuse twice — the common reflex — and Android never shows it again. From then on the entire point of the app fails silently: partner messages, Reaches and incoming calls never notify, and nothing anywhere in the app tells the user that notifications are off or offers a way to fix it. Both partners will believe the other is ignoring them.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart:191 calls `FcmService.registerToken()` on first entry, which at mobile/lib/core/services/fcm_service.dart:153 does `await requestPermission()` → fcm_service.dart:131-133, a bare `FirebaseMessaging.instance.requestPermission()` with no preceding rationale dialog. There is no recovery UI: `grep -rn "areNotificationsEnabled|openNotificationSettings|Permission.notification" lib` returns zero hits, and the only notification row in Settings is "Pause notifications" (mobile/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart:780-784). Contrast the two permissions that *were* done right: LocationService.onboard (mobile/lib/core/services/location_service.dart:242-257) explains first, and the Home screen carries a repair notice (home_screen.dart:255-312); FsiPermission.promptIfNeeded (mobile/lib/core/services/fsi_permission.dart:62-72) explains first.
fix: Wrap the FCM request in the same rationale dialog the location and FSI flows already use, ask it as part of the sequenced first-run chain, and add a persistent "Notifications are off — your partner's messages won't reach you" band on Home plus a Settings row that opens the system notification page, mirroring `_LocationBlockedNotice`.

title: Four modals fire at once the moment a new user enters the app, one of them asking for their password again
userImpact: The first thing a stranger sees inside Miles is a pile-up: the Android notification dialog, a "Let calls ring on your lock screen" dialog, a "Protect your memories — type your password" dialog, and a location dialog, all racing. They dismiss whichever is on top without reading it, which is exactly how a permission gets permanently denied. Worse, a dialog demanding the account password within a minute of sign-up is indistinguishable from a phishing screen — the escrow file's own doc comment says so.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart `_onReady()`: line 191 `FcmService.registerToken()` (fires the system notification dialog), line 199 `unawaited(EscrowPrompt.maybeShow(context))`, line 223 `_firstRunPrompts(couple.id)` — none awaited relative to each other. `_firstRunPrompts` (app_shell.dart:266-278) carefully sequences only two of the four, with a comment that names the exact failure: "Fired in parallel they land on top of one another and the user dismisses whichever is in front — which is how a permission ask gets refused without ever being read." The escrow prompt fires for every new signup: with email confirmation on, `signUp` returns no session so escrow is never written (mobile/lib/core/data/supabase_repository.dart:129-133 — `if (res.session == null) return;`), and the user reaches the app via the confirmation link without ever passing through `signIn()`, so `KeyEscrow.isMissing()` (mobile/lib/core/data/key_escrow.dart:176-191) is true. The dialog's own header warns it "is indistinguishable from a phishing screen" (mobile/lib/core/widgets/escrow_prompt.dart:18-21).
fix: Put all four in the one awaited chain `_firstRunPrompts` already is, spread across sessions rather than one burst, and move the escrow ask off first-run entirely — seal the key on the confirmation-link sign-in (where the password is still in hand) or defer the prompt until the user first opens the Vault.

title: The Vault PIN has no recovery — forget it and the contents are gone forever
userImpact: A 4-digit PIN, set on first open with no warning that it cannot be recovered, guarding the user's private photos. Forget it and there is no reset, no "Forgot PIN?", no path through the account password — just "Wrong PIN" forever, then a 15-minute lockout. That is a support email you cannot answer. The app already knows this is wrong: the *other* PIN gate in the same app has a full recovery flow.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/vault/vault_gate_screen.dart:250-322 — `_GateBody` renders title, subtitle, PinPad and (only when a PIN exists) a biometrics button. There is no forgot/reset control anywhere in the file. `grep -rn "Forgot" lib` finds exactly two: the password reset on sign_in_page.dart:189, and Memory Threads' own recovery — mobile/lib/features/closer/memory_threads/memory_threads_screen.dart:99 `_forgotPin()` and :355 the "Forgot your PIN?" button, whose doc comment at :88 says "no 'forgot' affordance anywhere, so the only escape from four forgotten digits...". The vault never got the same treatment. This is also the repo's own open task #6, "Honest failures + PIN recovery".
fix: Reuse the Memory Threads pattern verbatim on the vault gate: a "Forgot your PIN?" link that requires the account password (`SupabaseRepository.reauthenticate`) and then lets the user set a new PIN. Also state on the setup screen that the PIN cannot be recovered any other way.
effort: S — the flow already exists one directory over

title: Turning on Closer without a partner leaves the tab as a spinner that never stops
userImpact: Flip the "Closer" switch in Settings while your partner has not joined yet (or after they disconnect) and the Closer tab shows a bare loading spinner forever. No text, no explanation, no retry button, no way to tell whether the app is broken or thinking. The switch that caused it does not warn you and is not disabled.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/closer/closer_screen.dart:45-47 — `if (couple == null || couple.modestMode || me == null || partner == null) { return; }` returns *before* any `setState`, so `_key` stays at its initial `_KeyState.loading` (declared :30). Build then takes closer_screen.dart:112-114 — `case _KeyState.loading: return const Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator());`. Nothing ever re-runs it except `didChangeDependencies`. The toggle that reaches this state is ungated: mobile/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart:686-699 — `onChanged: _busy ? null : _toggleModestMode`, with no partner check.
fix: Add a `_KeyState.noPartner` branch that renders the existing `_WaitingForPartner` widget (it is already in the file at :181), and disable the Settings switch with an explanatory subtitle until a partner exists.

title: The shared photo gallery — and eight other features — are locked behind the intimacy switch
userImpact: "Gallery — everything, shared" is the single most expected feature of a couples app, and a new couple cannot reach it. It lives only inside the Closer tab, which is off by default and stays off until someone finds a switch in Settings labelled "Closer / Hidden. Reveal for both partners." Nobody looking for a photo album would guess that. Today's view, the watch list, wish jar and memory threads are behind the same door. The side drawer — the app's only other feature menu — does not list any of them.
evidence: `grep -rn "'/app/gallery'" lib` returns exactly two hits: the route definition (mobile/lib/core/app/router.dart:334) and mobile/lib/features/closer/closer_screen.dart:338 — the Closer grid tile. Same for `/app/routines` (closer_screen.dart:344) and `/app/watch-list` (closer_screen.dart:350). The gate: `modest_mode boolean not null default true` (supabase/migrations/20260601001200_intimacy_additions.sql:14), read at mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart:388 and closer_screen.dart:93, which renders `_ModestModeOn` ("It stays off until both of you turn it on in Settings", closer_screen.dart:163). Live prod confirms only one couple has ever flipped it. The drawer's 12 tiles (mobile/lib/features/shell/app_drawer.dart:104-205) contain no Gallery entry.
fix: Move Gallery, Today and Watch list out of Closer — they are not intimate features. Put Gallery in the bottom nav or at the top of the drawer where a new couple will find it on day one, and leave Closer for the things that genuinely need the opt-in.

title: The back arrow on the very first screen does nothing
userImpact: A visible, tappable back arrow sits in the top-left of the sign-in screen — the first thing a stranger sees. Tapping it navigates to the same screen. Nothing moves. It reads as a frozen app in the first five seconds.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/auth/sign_in_page.dart:135 — `onBack: () => context.go('/')`. mobile/lib/core/app/router.dart:364-367 — `GoRoute(path: '/', redirect: (_, __) => '/signin')`. AuthScaffold renders the arrow whenever `onBack != null` (mobile/lib/features/auth/widgets/auth_scaffold.dart, the `if (onBack != null) IconButton(...)` block), and its own doc says "a screen with no way back should show no control, rather than one that does nothing" — which is exactly what happens here.
fix: Pass `onBack: null` on SignInPage when there is nowhere to go back to, or point it at the new intro screen once that exists.

title: An onboarding path for the disguise picker exists, is unreachable, and a comment claims it runs
userImpact: No direct user impact today, but it is half-built code behind a door nobody can open, and a comment in the shell asserts it is running when it is not — which is how the next person "fixes" the wrong thing.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart:267 — "The cover question is NOT here any more — it runs from `_onReady` before the couple check, so an unpaired user still gets asked." It does not: `_onReady` (app_shell.dart:184-224) contains no such call, and `grep -rn "onboarding=1|isOnboarding" lib` finds the query parameter only in the route definition (mobile/lib/core/app/router.dart:209) and in the screen that consumes it (mobile/lib/features/disguise/disguise_picker_screen.dart:21, :99, :136, :190, :197). Nothing anywhere navigates to `/app/disguise?onboarding=1`.
fix: Either delete the `isOnboarding` branch from disguise_picker_screen.dart or correct the comment in app_shell.dart. Leaving both is the worst of the three options.

title: A new message produces no notification of any kind — and the code that would show one is dead
userImpact: A stranger installs the app, their partner sends a message, and the phone never lights up. No banner, no sound, no badge — nothing, ever, on any device. There is no setting to turn it on. They will assume the app is broken, or that their partner never wrote. This is the single most expected behaviour in the category and it is absent.
evidence: Live prod: `select pg_get_functiondef('notify_message'::regproc) like '%msg_sync%'` -> true, `like '%''message''%'` -> false. The trigger `message_notify_on_insert` on `public.messages` therefore only ever emits kind `msg_sync`. Both client handlers deliberately draw nothing for it: mobile/lib/core/services/reach_notifications.dart:412-422 ("it draws NOTHING. No channel, no notification, no sound, no badge") and mobile/lib/core/services/fcm_service.dart:266-287 ("No notification... the push is here to move the tick, nothing else"). `showMessageNotification` (mobile/lib/core/services/reach_notifications.dart:209) has exactly one caller — reach_notifications.dart:433, inside the `type == 'message'` branch — and no producer sends that kind any more, so it is dead code behind a removed trigger. Settings offers only "Pause notifications" (mobile/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart:784); grep for any other notification control in settings_screen.dart returns nothing.
fix: This was a deliberate choice for a two-phone install and it does not survive contact with strangers. Keep the owner's preference as a *default he can set on his own handset*, not as the product: add a `message` push kind alongside `msg_sync` (a new kind, so shipped clients ignore it), wire it to the existing `showMessageNotification`, and add a Settings toggle "New message notifications" defaulting ON. Gate the server send on that per-user column so the owner can switch his own off. Do not reuse the old `message` kind name — build 41-and-older clients would start banner-ing.
effort: 1-2 days: one column, one branch in notify_message/reach-notify, one settings row, one already-written notification builder.

title: An uncaught throw in push registration silently kills every notification on that device
userImpact: On an affected phone the user gets no incoming-call ring while the app is closed, no Reach, no Care nudge, no memory proposal, and no delivery acks — permanently, and with zero feedback. It re-fires on every app resume, so it never self-heals. This already happened to one of the two real users on the current build.
evidence: mobile/lib/core/services/fcm_service.dart:153 — `await requestPermission();` sits outside any try/catch, while every line after it (the 4-attempt `getToken()` loop, `_save(token)`, and the `onTokenRefresh` listener hook at :162-165) is unreachable once it throws. Live prod `client_errors` id 115, user 8f9461d9, build 42, 2026-08-17 00:52: `FirebaseException` with stack `#3 MethodChannelFirebaseMessaging.requestPermission -> #4 FcmService.requestPermission (core/services/fcm_service.dart:132) -> #5 FcmService.registerToken (core/services/fcm_service.dart:153)`. Both call sites are fire-and-forget with no `.catchError`: mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart:191 and mobile/lib/main.dart:378. The method's own doc comment at fcm_service.dart:137-143 states that re-saving on each foreground is what self-heals a token the notify functions nulled as UNREGISTERED — that self-heal is exactly what this throw disables.
fix: Wrap `await requestPermission()` in try/catch and continue to the token fetch regardless (permission denial and a plugin fault must not block registration). Separately, give both call sites a `.catchError` so a future throw anywhere in `registerToken` cannot take the whole path down unobserved. Then verify by confirming `profiles.fcm_token` updates after a resume on a handset that reproduced the exception.
effort: 30 minutes to fix; the verification needs one device that reproduces it.

title: The vault PIN has no recovery — forgetting it locks you out of your own vault forever
userImpact: A user sets a 4-digit PIN on the private vault, forgets it, and there is no way back in. No "Forgot PIN", no email reset, no sign-out-and-back-in escape. After 5 wrong attempts they are locked out for 15 minutes and then face the same wall. Their photos and notes are still on the server and they can never see them again.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/vault/vault_gate_screen.dart contains no reset affordance — `grep -rni "forgot|reset" lib/features/vault/*.dart` returns exactly one hit, a comment at vault_gate_screen.dart:32 about resetting the keypad widget. Live prod function list for the whole vault surface: `has_vault_pin`, `set_vault_pin`, `verify_vault_pin` — no reset RPC exists. `verify_vault_pin` body (live): `locked_until = case when failed_attempts + 1 >= 5 then now() + interval '15 minutes' end`. The repo's own task list still carries "#6 [pending] Honest failures + PIN recovery".
fix: The server side already supports it: `set_vault_pin` is `on conflict (user_id) do update set pin_hash = excluded.pin_hash, failed_attempts = 0, locked_until = null` — it overwrites without needing the old PIN. So a "Forgot PIN" row on the gate that re-authenticates the user (re-enter account password, or biometric) and then calls `setPin` is a UI-only change. Decide and state the consequence plainly on that screen — since vault files are encrypted under the account key, not the PIN, resetting the PIN loses nothing, and users should be told that so they do not fear it.

title: One of the two real users has no key backup — a reinstall destroys their history silently
userImpact: That user reinstalls the app, or taps "Clear data", and every encrypted memory, vault file and Closer item becomes permanently unreadable to them. Nothing warns them beforehand and nothing explains it afterwards. At a 1-in-2 rate on the only real accounts that exist, a meaningful share of new couples will hit this.
evidence: Live prod: `select p.id, (select count(*) from key_escrow k where k.user_id=p.id) escrow_rows, (select count(*) from partner_keys pk where pk.user_id=p.id) key_rows from profiles p` returns user 8bfaaeb3-71c5-4278-9aff-d1806c9ee26a with `key_rows=1, escrow_rows=0` — a published X25519 identity with no sealed backup of the seed. The other paired user 8f9461d9 has 1 and 1. Totals: `key_escrow` 1 row against 3 accounts / 2 paired. The owner flagged this himself in docs/guides/BRAIN.md §35 ("One partner has no recovery path — reinstall and that key is gone... Not investigated this turn") and it is still true. Backup is only ever attempted at sign-up (mobile/lib/core/data/supabase_repository.dart:133) and sign-in (:208), and sign-up returns early at :128 when email confirmation is on (`if (res.session == null) return;`), so a user who confirms by link and never signs in again never gets one.
fix: Find out which of the two write paths did not fire for 8bfaaeb3 before writing any code — the account is still live and reproducible. Then make the gap visible rather than silent: `KeyEscrow.isMissing()` already exists (key_escrow.dart:171) and mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart:196-198 already reasons about this case, so surface a one-time, non-dismissable prompt asking for the password when it returns true. Add a negative test that a fresh confirm-by-email signup ends with exactly one escrow row.

title: Vault notes are stored in plaintext under a UI that promises "only you can ever read this"
userImpact: The user types a private note into a PIN-locked vault, reading a hint that says nobody else can ever read it, and the note goes to the database as readable text. Vault *files* are genuinely encrypted, so the app is inconsistent with itself. This is the sentence that ends up in a screenshot next to a database row.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/vault/vault_repository.dart:126-133 — `addNote` does `_c.from('personal_vault_items').insert({'owner_id': uid, 'type': 'note', 'content': content})` with no encryption step. Compare the file path in the same class: `_refuseCleartext(packedFull)` at :216 and the guard itself at :266. The claims: mobile/lib/features/vault/vault_screen.dart:256 `hintText: 'Just for you — only you can ever read this'`, :494 `'Your vault is empty.\nAdd a private note only you can see.'`, and mobile/lib/features/vault/vault_gate_screen.dart:285-287 `'A 4-digit PIN protects what only you can see.'` / `'Your partner can never open this.'`. BRAIN.md §37 records the Terms being corrected to disclose this — the disclosure was fixed, the behaviour was not.
fix: Encrypt the note body the same way the vault already encrypts file bytes — `CryptoCore.encryptBytesOffThread` over the UTF-8 note, stored in `content` with the existing packed format, and decrypt on read. It is the same primitive already in the same file. Until that lands, the two hint strings must stop claiming exclusivity.
effort: 1 day, plus a read-path migration for any existing plaintext notes (currently zero rows in prod, so this is the cheapest it will ever be).

title: Four headline features have never once been used in production — by anyone, including the developer
userImpact: Watch Together, Memory Threads, the private Vault and the Timeline are front-and-centre in how this app is described, and there is no evidence any of them has ever completed a single real run. The first person to try them will be a stranger. "It works on the developer's phone" is not merely weak evidence here — it is unavailable.
evidence: Live prod row counts across the database's entire lifetime: `watch_sessions` 0, `memory_threads` 0, `personal_vault_items` 0, `visits` 0 (the timeline's table). For contrast, the features that have been exercised: `gallery_items` 22, `reach_events` 15, `call_invites` 6, `turn_mints` 3. Note the prod wipe (BRAIN §29) was on 2026-08-16 and the two testers signed up fresh after it, so these zeroes cover the whole post-wipe period in which both handsets have been active.
fix: Before any Play submission, run each of the four end-to-end on two handsets and record the row counts moving. These are also the four highest-risk screens precisely because they are unexercised — expect the failures to be in first-run and empty-state handling, which is where nothing has ever been observed. Watch Together in particular carries a WebView that permits same-host navigation (mobile/lib/features/watch/watch_viewer.dart:30-46), so it needs a real session before a reviewer finds one.
effort: 1 day of structured manual testing, no code assumed.

title: There is no way to search the chat
userImpact: The product's core value is a couple's shared history, and there is no way to find anything in it. Wanting to find "that restaurant you mentioned" is a daily need, and every messaging app the user has ever used has a search icon in the chat header. Its absence reads as an unfinished app.
evidence: `grep -rni "search" mobile/lib/features/chat/` returns hits only inside the Giphy picker (mobile/lib/features/chat/widgets/giphy_picker.dart:29-93) — nothing in chat_screen.dart, chat_repository.dart, or any chat widget. There is no search route, no search field, and no query path.
fix: Message bodies are ciphertext server-side, so this cannot be a Postgres `ilike`. Search the locally decrypted message cache the chat already maintains, scoped to what is paged in, and be explicit in the UI that it searches messages on this device. That is what Signal does for the same reason, and it is honest about the constraint rather than promising a server search the encryption forbids.
effort: 2-3 days for a device-local search over the existing cache.

title: No "Change password" anywhere in the app
userImpact: A signed-in user who wants to change their password cannot. They must sign out, tap "Forgot password", wait for an email, and follow a link. Every account-based app has this in Settings, and its absence is the kind of thing a review calls out.
evidence: `SupabaseRepository.updatePassword` exists at mobile/lib/core/data/supabase_repository.dart:290 but its only caller is mobile/lib/features/auth/new_password_page.dart, and the router serves `/new-password` only for a recovery-link session (mobile/lib/core/app/router.dart:78-79: "A recovery link signs the user in with a short-lived session... Recovery outranks the funnel"). Settings has Gender, How this app looks, Full-screen alerts, Closer, Biometric app lock, Pause notifications, Report a problem, Sign out, Delete account — and no password row (mobile/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart:556-832).
fix: Add a Settings → Account → Change password row that reuses the existing `updatePassword` path, including its `PasswordChangeOutcome` handling. This matters more here than in a typical app: per BRAIN §38, the account password is also the escrow wrap secret (Argon2id over the raw password), so `updatePassword` already re-seals the escrow row — which means the *only* code path that keeps escrow in step with the password is currently unreachable except by email reset.
effort: Half a day; the repository method and its outcome enum already exist.

title: The disguise picker tells Play users something false about their own phone
userImpact: A user picks a cover for privacy reasons and reads a reassurance that Android's app list will keep calling the app "News". On the Play build it says "Miles". They check, find their real app name sitting in Settings, and now distrust the privacy feature they just turned on — which is worse than never having claimed it.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/disguise/disguise_picker_screen.dart:176-178: "Android's own Settings › Apps list keeps calling this app \"News\" whichever disguise you pick. That name is fixed when the app is installed and no app can change it afterwards." But mobile/android/app/src/play/AndroidManifest.xml:26 sets `android:label="Miles"` on `<application>` and :37 sets it on the main activity. The picker is reachable on Play: mobile/android/app/build.gradle.kts:152 sets `DISGUISE_ENABLED = true` for the play flavour (the Option C decision in BRAIN §34). The owner recorded this as "found, not fixed" in BRAIN §38 item 5 and it is still open.
fix: Make the copy read the flavour rather than assert a constant — on play, say the app list shows "Miles"; on sideload, "News". Both facts are already available at build time via the same BuildConfig field that gates the screen.

title: A plugin crash reaches the top-level error handler on the two newest builds, and the report cannot say which plugin
userImpact: Something the app depends on fails to register on a real user's phone and whatever it powers is dead there. Nobody can tell what, because the crash report deliberately drops the message. The owner will get a support email he cannot act on.
evidence: Live prod `client_errors` id 116 (build 42, user 8f9461d9, 2026-08-17 01:17) and id 114 (build 41, same user): `MissingPluginException` with stack `#0 MethodChannel._invokeMethod -> #1 EventChannel.receiveBroadcastStream.<anonymous closure>`. `grep -rn "EventChannel|receiveBroadcastStream" mobile/lib/` returns zero hits, so the failing channel belongs to a plugin, not app code. The channel name is in `error.toString()`, which mobile/lib/core/diag/diag.dart:96-101 discards by design — `_detail` returns non-null only for PostgrestException, AuthException and SocketException, which is why all 21 rows in `client_errors` have `detail = null`.
fix: The redaction policy at diag.dart:83-95 is sound and should stay. But `MissingPluginException` carries a channel name and no user data, so add it to the typed `_detail` switch alongside the other three. That turns an unactionable report into a named plugin on the next occurrence. Until then this is UNVERIFIED as to which feature is affected — the device that produced it is still available to reproduce against.
effort: 1 hour for the reporter change; diagnosis follows the next occurrence.

title: A chat app that never tells you a message arrived — and the code to do it is built, complete, and unreachable
userImpact: Partner sends a message. The recipient's phone shows nothing: no banner, no sound, no badge, no dot on the Chat tab, no count anywhere. They find out only if they happen to open the app and tap Chat. Nothing in the app, the FAQ, or onboarding says this is intentional. Every stranger will file it as "notifications are broken" — it is the #1 review a messaging app gets when this is wrong.
evidence: Server sends kind `msg_sync` (supabase/functions/reach-notify/index.ts:218, 229, 314). Background handler: `if (type == 'msg_sync') { ... it draws NOTHING. No channel, no notification, no sound, no badge` — mobile/lib/core/services/reach_notifications.dart:409-419. Foreground: `// No notification. ... the owner does not want message banners` — mobile/lib/core/services/fcm_service.dart (_onForeground, msg_sync branch). The working implementation exists and is dead: `showMessageNotification` (reach_notifications.dart:209) + `buildMsgChannel` (reach_notifications.dart:195) are reachable only from the `type == 'message'` branch at reach_notifications.dart:433, and the server never sends that string. In-app fallback also absent: `grep -rn "unread" lib/` returns zero UI matches; mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart:439-468 builds NavigationDestinations with no Badge.
fix: Two choices, both cheap. (a) Switch it on: send `message` instead of `msg_sync` (or add the branch), add a Settings → Notifications section with a Messages toggle defaulting ON, keep the current content-free notification body so the disguise holds. (b) Keep it off but stop it reading as a bug: add an unread count on the Chat tab AND a first-run screen plus an FAQ entry saying "Miles does not notify you about messages — by design." (a) is what strangers expect; do (a) and let the user turn it off.
effort: ~1 day (channel, notification and payload router already written and tested)

title: Chat history is capped at the newest 300 messages, with no way to load older ones
userImpact: After ~300 messages — two to three weeks of daily chatting — everything older is invisible, permanently. The messages are still on the server; the app simply has no path to them. Scrolling to the top hits a wall with no spinner and no "load earlier" affordance. "The app deleted a year of our conversation" is the review, and it is an app about keeping a relationship's history.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/chat/chat_repository.dart:335-341 — `fetch()` is `.order('created_at', ascending: false).limit(300)`. No pagination exists anywhere in the feature: `grep -rn "loadMore|fetchOlder|olderThan|range(|\.lt('seq'|\.lt('created_at'" lib/features/chat/` returns nothing. The only scroll listener, chat_screen.dart:699-704, handles the new-message pill only. The other read path, `fetchSince` (chat_repository.dart:304-311), is forward-only — the window slides newer and never back. Contrast mobile/lib/features/profile/shared_media_repository.dart:44-64, which paginates correctly with `beforeSeq` — the pattern already exists in the codebase and chat does not use it.
fix: Copy the `shared_media_repository.page(beforeSeq:)` pattern into `ChatRepository`: add `fetchBefore(coupleId, beforeSeq, limit)`, and in `_onScroll` fire it when the reverse ListView nears `maxScrollExtent`, with a small header spinner. Cap page size at 100.

title: Applying a launcher cover shows the WRONG unlock gesture — a one-tap, irreversible lockout
userImpact: User picks the Calculator cover. The confirmation dialog — the last thing they read before their app disappears from the launcher — tells them: "tap the logo 5 times quickly or press and hold the 'Local' tab for about 3 seconds." A calculator has no logo and no Local tab. The real gesture is "Hold = while the display reads 0." They confirm, the app becomes a calculator, and the only instructions they were ever given are for a different app. They cannot get back in. The success snackbar does not repeat the gesture either. This is not a rough edge; it is a way to lose your account with two taps and no warning.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/disguise/disguise_picker_screen.dart:52-59 — the dialog content is a hardcoded const string: `'To get back in: open it, then tap the logo 5 times quickly or press and hold the "Local" tab for about 3 seconds.'` It never reads `choice.entry`. The correct per-cover strings exist at mobile/lib/features/disguise/disguise_profile.dart:108-181 (`'Hold = while the display reads 0...'`, `'Hold the battery ring.'`, `'Hold the angle readout with the phone lying flat.'`, …) and are rendered in the picker row at disguise_picker_screen.dart:283. The hardcoded text does not even match the News profile's own entry string ('Five taps on the masthead mark, top left.'). Success snackbar (disguise_picker_screen.dart:93-97) says only 'This app is now "X".' Separately, mobile/android/app/build.gradle.kts:141-147 lists as a hard requirement for shipping the play flavour: "3. a visible way out on every cover screen" — `grep -rn -i "way out|exit|open miles" lib/features/disguise/covers/ lib/features/covers/` finds no implementation.
fix: Two lines: interpolate `${choice.entry}` into the dialog, and repeat it in the success snackbar. Then satisfy the owner's own gate item 3 — either a universal fallback (long-press anywhere on a cover for 3s → PIN prompt) or a persistent notification-tray shortcut. Also add a test asserting the dialog string contains `choice.entry` for every profile.
effort: ~15 min for the dialog; ~half day for the universal way out

title: When the chat cannot load, the app shows the brand-new-couple empty state
userImpact: Airplane mode, dead Wi-Fi, Supabase paused, an RLS change, a bad token — any of these, and the user opens Chat and reads: "💌 Say something sweet. This is your private space — just the two of you. Send the first message." To a couple with months of history, the app is telling them their conversation is gone. There is no error, no retry, no "couldn't connect". This is the single most alarming failure mode in the app and it fires on the most ordinary event there is: a phone with no signal.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/chat/chat_screen.dart:729-735 — `try { final msgs = await ChatRepository.fetch(...); ... } catch (_) { // first-run is fine }`, then line 738 unconditionally `setState(() => _loading = false)`, and chat_screen.dart:1544-1545 renders `_EmptyChat()` whenever `_messages.isEmpty`. `_EmptyChat` is the copy quoted above (chat_screen.dart:2682-2709). There is no local message cache — pubspec.yaml lists no sqflite/hive/drift/isar and no connectivity package — so an offline open always lands here. This also violates the repo's own "no silent failures" rule.
fix: Catch into a `_loadError` field and render three distinct states: loaded-and-empty (current copy), load-failed ("Couldn't load your messages — check your connection" + Retry button), and loading. Optionally cache the last page to SharedPreferences/disk so an offline open shows history read-only.
effort: ~2 hours for the honest state; ~1 day if you add the offline cache

title: Sign-up requires a confirmation email the project cannot reliably send
userImpact: Supabase's built-in mailer is a shared dev sender rate-limited to roughly 2-4 messages per hour, project-wide. With confirmations required, the 3rd person to sign up in an hour never receives their email and simply cannot create an account — and neither can anyone requesting a password reset in the same window. From the user's side nothing is wrong: the app says "check your email" and the email never comes. On a Play launch this caps you at a handful of new users per hour on day one.
evidence: supabase/config.toml:56 — `enable_confirmations = true`; there is no `[auth.email.smtp]` block anywhere in the file (`sed -n '35,70p' supabase/config.toml`). The repo already flags this twice: docs/guides/BRAIN.md:2381 ("No `[auth.email.smtp]` block in config.toml, so the shared built-in sender is in use") and BRAIN.md:4038 ("auth email delivery depends on built-in SMTP (~2-4/hr dev cap — custom SMTP unverified, dashboard-only)"). All 3 live accounts are confirmed (`select email_confirmed_at is not null from auth.users` → all true), consistent with confirmations being on. UNVERIFIED: the production project's SMTP setting is dashboard-side and not readable over SQL — what settles it is Supabase Dashboard → Project Settings → Authentication → SMTP Settings showing a custom provider, or sending 5 signups in 5 minutes to real inboxes and counting arrivals.
fix: Configure custom SMTP on sopictusdonlvuezmfep before launch (Resend/Postmark/SES — a verified sending domain plus SPF/DKIM). Do NOT solve it by turning confirmations off: that lets anyone register someone else's address. Then send 5 signups in 5 minutes and paste the arrivals as proof.

title: There is no search — not for a message, not for a photo, not for anything
userImpact: "What was that restaurant you mentioned?" — the user has no way to find out except scrolling, and past 300 messages scrolling doesn't reach it either. Same for the shared Gallery, the Timeline, Memory Threads and the Vault. WhatsApp, Signal and Telegram all put a search icon in the chat app bar; its absence in an app whose entire purpose is a shared history will read as unfinished.
evidence: `grep -rn -il "search" lib/` returns 8 files, and every one is unrelated: giphy_service.dart / giphy_picker.dart (GIF search), chat_input_bar.dart (the GIF field), news_cover_screen.dart + convert_cover.dart + cover_gate.dart (the disguise covers), faq_text.dart (prose), settings_screen.dart:1219-1225 (the timezone picker's city filter). No search field exists in chat_screen.dart, gallery_screen.dart, timeline_screen.dart or vault_screen.dart. Server side there is no text index either — `select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name='messages'` shows no tsvector column.
fix: Ship chat text search first — it is the one everyone looks for. Add a tsvector column plus GIN index on `messages.body`, an app-bar search icon, results list, and tap-to-jump (which needs the pagination from the history finding, so do them together). Gallery/Timeline search can wait.
effort: ~2-3 days for chat search including the jump-to-message

title: Calls leave no trace — no history, no missed-call record anywhere
userImpact: Partner calls while the phone is face-down. The notification times out and disappears. There is nothing in the app that says a call happened — no Calls tab, no "Missed call" bubble in the chat, no badge. The user has no idea they were called; the caller has no idea whether it rang. Every calling app on the planet records this.
evidence: `ls lib/features/call/` → call_controller.dart, call_foreground.dart, call_pip.dart, call_screen.dart, call_stats.dart, pip_mode.dart. No list/history screen. `grep -rn -i "missed call|call history|callLog|recent calls" lib/` returns one comment only (call_controller.dart:406). Calls write to `call_invites` (call_controller.dart:317) and that row is deleted on hangup (call_controller.dart:361) and pruned after 2 days by `prune_ephemera` (live cron job 5: `delete from public.call_invites where created_at < now() - interval '2 days'`). The `messages` table has no call/system kind — `kind` is parsed with fallback 'text' (chat_repository.dart:66) and the only handled kinds are text/image/video/voice/file.
fix: Cheapest version that covers it: on call end (or ring timeout), insert a `kind: 'call'` message row carrying direction, duration and answered/missed, and render it as a system bubble in the chat. That gives history, missed calls and "call back" in one place with no new screen.

title: Screen readers get nothing on the app's primary controls
userImpact: A blind or low-vision user opens Chat and TalkBack announces the send/mic button as nothing at all — it is an unlabeled box. Same for the home screen's main actions. The app is effectively unusable with a screen reader, and Play's accessibility guidance plus a growing number of reviewers check exactly this.
evidence: 11 semantics usages across 238 Dart files: `grep -rn "Semantics(|semanticLabel|semanticsLabel|excludeSemantics" lib/ | wc -l` → 11, in 9 files (none of them chat_screen.dart, home_screen.dart, gallery_screen.dart, settings_screen.dart). The most-used control in the app — mobile/lib/features/chat/widgets/chat_input_bar.dart:562-583 — is a bare `GestureDetector` wrapping a `Container` wrapping an `Icon`, with no tooltip, no Semantics and no label; it is send, mic-record and stop depending on state, and announces none of them. home_screen.dart:358 and :446 are likewise bare GestureDetectors. UNVERIFIED (needs a device run): behaviour at 150-200% system font scale — nothing in the app clamps or overrides textScaler (`grep -rn "textScaleFactor|textScaler|TextScaler" lib/` → no matches, which is the correct default), but there are 97 hardcoded `height: NN,` values under lib/features/, several around text; settle it by running with Android's largest display/font size and screenshotting Chat, Home and Settings.
fix: Wrap the send/mic button in `Semantics(button: true, label: _recording ? 'Stop recording' : _hasText ? 'Send message' : 'Hold to record a voice note')`. Then sweep every bare GestureDetector/InkWell around an icon in chat, home, gallery and closer and give it a label — IconButtons with tooltips are already covered, so this is a bounded list. Then do one pass at 200% font scale.

title: No way to change your password or your email from inside the app
userImpact: A user who wants to change their password — because it leaked, because a partner learned it, because it's good hygiene — cannot. They have to sign out, tap "Forgot password?", and go through an email round trip on the mailer described above. Changing an email address is impossible at any price: an account is welded to the address it was created with. Every account-based app has both in Settings.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart — full file read; the Account section (lines 817-835) contains exactly two items: Sign out and Delete account. No password row, no email row. `SupabaseRepository.updatePassword` (supabase_repository.dart:290) has exactly one caller: `lib/features/auth/new_password_page.dart:72`, which is only reachable from a recovery-link session. `grep -rn "changeEmail|setEmail|UserAttributes(email" lib/` → no matches; email change is not implemented at all.
fix: Add Settings → Account → "Change password" (current password → new password), calling the existing `updatePassword`, which already re-seals the key escrow and returns a `PasswordChangeOutcome` you can surface honestly. Email change needs `updateUser(UserAttributes(email:))` plus the double-confirm flow config.toml already enables (`double_confirm_changes = true`).
effort: ~half day for password; ~1 day for email

title: On the Play build, the forced-update screen is a dead end with no button
userImpact: The moment you raise `app_release.min_build` — the mechanism you built specifically so breaking changes are safe — every Play user is dropped onto a full-screen block with an icon, a sentence, and nothing to tap. No "Open in Play Store", no back, no sign out. The message currently in production even says "Install the latest build", which is sideload language on a store app. The user's only recourse is to guess that they should go find the app in Play themselves.
evidence: mobile/lib/main.dart:723-770 — the block screen's only action is `if (UpdateService.available) ...[ ElevatedButton ]`. mobile/lib/core/services/update_service.dart:57-60 — `available => allowed && ...`, and `allowed` reads the `SELF_UPDATE` BuildConfig flag, which mobile/android/app/build.gradle.kts:159 sets to `false` on the play flavour. So on Play the button is never rendered. Live row confirms it is armed: `select * from app_release` → `min_build: 42, latest_build: 43, message: "This version is out of date. Install the latest build to keep your photos and messages working."`. The table is a single row (`id: true`) shared by both channels, so raising it for sideload blocks Play users too — already noted at docs/guides/BRAIN.md:4036-4038.
fix: On the play flavour, render an "Update in Play Store" button that launches `market://details?id=<pkg>` with an https fallback, plus a Sign out escape. And split `app_release` per channel (add a `channel` column, or a second row) so a sideload bump cannot brick Play. Rewrite the production `message` to be store-neutral.
effort: ~1 hour for the button; ~2 hours for the channel split

title: Nothing tells the user they are offline, and a failed send never retries itself
userImpact: Send a message in a lift or a tunnel: it fails and turns into a red bubble that sits there. When signal returns, nothing happens — the user must notice the failed bubble and tap it, per message. WhatsApp shows a clock and sends the moment the network is back. There is also no connection banner anywhere in the app, so every failure looks like an app bug rather than a network one.
evidence: pubspec.yaml lists no `connectivity_plus` or equivalent — the app never observes network state. mobile/lib/features/chat/chat_send_queue.dart:390-407 — on failure `send.status = SendStatus.failed` and the item stops; `_pump()` (line 379) only starts items already in `SendStatus.sending`. Recovery is manual only: `ChatSendQueue.instance.retry(id)` is called from chat_screen.dart:2341, chat_screen.dart:2603 and file_bubble.dart:78 — all user taps. No caller re-pumps on resume or on connectivity change (`grep -rn "ChatSendQueue.instance" lib/` — full list checked).
fix: Add `connectivity_plus`, and on the offline→online transition flip failed sends back to `sending` and call `_pump()`. Show a slim "No connection" bar under the app bar while offline. Also re-pump on app resume, which costs nothing and catches most cases on its own.

title: The shared photo album is capped at 500 and hidden behind a padlocked tab called "Closer"
userImpact: Two problems in one place. Discoverability: a user looking for "our photos" will not find them — the Gallery lives inside a bottom-tab labelled "Closer" wearing a padlock icon, beside Wish Jar and Mood Lamp. Nothing in the drawer or on Home points at it. Capacity: past 500 items the oldest photos become unreachable, same class of bug as the chat history cap.
evidence: mobile/lib/features/gallery/gallery_repository.dart:120-127 — `fetch()` is `.order('created_at', ascending: false).limit(500)` with no `beforeCreatedAt` parameter and no caller pagination. Entry point: `grep -rn "/app/gallery" lib/ | grep -v router.dart` returns exactly one hit — mobile/lib/features/closer/closer_screen.dart:338. The drawer (mobile/lib/features/shell/app_drawer.dart:110-202) lists 12 destinations and Gallery is not among them. The Closer tab renders `Icon(Icons.lock_outline)` with the label 'Closer' (app_shell.dart:461-468) and is gated on `showCloser = isAdult` (app_shell.dart:391), where `isAdult` is false whenever `birth_date` is null (models.dart:119-121) — so a profile that never completed onboarding loses the Gallery, Today, Watch List and Memory Threads entirely, with no explanation. Live prod has 22 gallery items.
fix: Paginate `GalleryRepository.fetch` with a `beforeCreatedAt` cursor. Add a "Photos" entry to the drawer pointing at `/app/gallery`, and/or a photo tile on Home. Consider moving Gallery, Today and Watch List out of Closer — they are not intimate features and do not belong behind the padlock.

title: No in-app way to reach a human — the support address is defined but never displayed
userImpact: A user who cannot sign in, or whose photos will not load, has no route to the developer from inside the app. "Report a problem" writes a row into a table nobody reads and gives no reply channel; the About card links FAQ, Terms, Privacy and Child Safety and no email. For a paid Play launch this becomes 1-star reviews used as a support channel, because reviews are the only channel that exists.
evidence: `const milesContactEmail = 'Razaaslam3210@gmail.com'` — mobile/lib/features/legal/terms_text.dart:53. `grep -rn "milesContactEmail" lib/ test/` returns 3 hits and none of them render it: terms_text.dart:40 (the `milesTermsHasContact` boolean), terms_text.dart:53 (the declaration) and test/unit/legal/terms_gate_test.dart:179. The About card (settings_screen.dart:957-999) shows four links, none an email. `showReportSheet` (lib/features/safety/safety_sheets.dart) posts to `submit_report` → `content_reports`, which has 0 rows in production and no admin surface; the sheet promises no response.
fix: Add Settings → About → "Contact support" opening a `mailto:` prefilled with build number, versionName and user id. Add the same line to the FAQ. If you want the report table to be real, add a Supabase Studio saved query or a weekly digest so someone actually reads it.

title: No message editing and no forwarding
userImpact: Send a typo and the only remedy is deleting the whole message and retyping it — WhatsApp, Signal and Telegram have all had edit for years and users now expect it. Forwarding is missing too: a photo or a link cannot be re-sent to the other chat surfaces (Memory Threads, Gallery, Watch List) without saving and re-uploading it by hand.
evidence: `grep -rn -i "edit message|editMessage|'Edit'|Forward|forwardTo" lib/` returns only unrelated matches (animation `.forward()` calls, a comment about forwarded links). The chat selection toolbar (chat_screen.dart:1483-1526) offers exactly Copy text, Reply, Report, Delete. `select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name='messages'` shows `updated_at` exists but no `edited_at`, and nothing writes an edit.
fix: Edit is the one worth doing: long-press → Edit on your own text messages inside a 15-minute window, `update messages set body=..., edited_at=now()`, render an "edited" marker. Skip forwarding for now — with one conversation there is nowhere to forward to.

title: Fonts are downloaded from Google at first launch, so a first run without signal renders in the wrong typeface
userImpact: Install on a plane, on hotel Wi-Fi with a captive portal, or on a phone that blocks Google endpoints, and the app's first impression is Roboto everywhere instead of Fraunces/Inter — different metrics, shifted layouts, an app that looks unfinished at exactly the moment it is being judged. It also means a network call to Google before the user has agreed to anything.
evidence: pubspec.yaml:28 declares `google_fonts: ^6.2.1` and pubspec.yaml has no `fonts:` section; `ls assets/fonts` → nothing bundled. 27 runtime call sites (`grep -rn "GoogleFonts\." lib/ | wc -l`), including the whole theme — mobile/lib/core/ui/theme.dart:111 (`GoogleFonts.fraunces`) and :115 (`GoogleFonts.inter`). `GoogleFonts.config.allowRuntimeFetching` is never set, so the package fetches from fonts.gstatic.com on first use. (Disclosure is fine — web/privacy-policy.html:355 and docs/legal/privacy-policy.md:214 both name Google Fonts.)
fix: Bundle the two families as assets, declare them in pubspec `fonts:`, and set `GoogleFonts.config.allowRuntimeFetching = false` in main() so a missed download can never silently degrade the app. Costs a few hundred KB in the AAB and removes a launch-time network dependency.

title: Supabase is on the FREE plan; measured usage fills its 1 GB storage cap in roughly 15 couple-days
userImpact: When project storage fills, storage uploads start failing for EVERY couple at once — photos, videos, voice notes, vault items. The app has no per-account quota and no code path that handles a full bucket, so users get generic upload failures with no explanation. This is not a scaling worry for later; it is a wall the app hits during the first week of a Play launch.
evidence: get_organization(fpmfuptznczuuksqybnx) → {"plan":"free"}. Free plan quotas (supabase.com/pricing): 1 GB file storage, 500 MB database, 5 GB egress, 2M realtime messages/mo, 200 peak realtime connections. Live query: `select bucket_id, count(*), sum((metadata->>'size')::bigint) from storage.objects group by 1` → couple_intimate 47 objects/51 MB, couple_media 50 objects/17 MB. `select min(created_at), max(created_at), sum(...) from storage.objects` → 97 objects, 70,688,097 bytes (67.4 MB), first 2026-08-16 15:54:44, last 2026-08-17 01:18:02 — all of it inside one 9.5-hour window, from ONE couple. Even discounting that tenfold as a heavy test day, 1 GB is ~150 couple-days. `pg_database_size` already 33 MB of the 500 MB DB cap, of which `diag_events` is 13 MB of bloat holding 0 live rows. grep for quota|storage_used|max_storage|usage_bytes across supabase/migrations and mobile/lib → no per-account quota anywhere.
fix: Two things, in order. (1) Move to Pro ($25/mo: 100 GB storage then $0.0213/GB, 250 GB egress then $0.09/GB, 8 GB disk) before a single stranger installs — the free plan is not a launch configuration. (2) Add a per-couple storage budget enforced server-side (a `couple_storage_usage` row maintained by a storage trigger, checked in an edge function before signing an upload), plus a media retention policy for chat originals. Also `VACUUM FULL public.diag_events` to reclaim the 13 MB.
effort: Plan upgrade: minutes. Quota + retention: 2-3 days.

title: An incoming chat message can be dropped permanently and silently — the id is marked seen before the message is stored
userImpact: Her message never appears. Not late — never, until the app is force-killed and relaunched. Every subsequent re-delivery (realtime insert, socket-reconnect catch-up, cold catch-up) sees the id in the seen-set and returns early as a duplicate. For a chat app this is the single worst possible defect, and the sender's screen still shows it as delivered.
evidence: chat_screen.dart:832 `_ids.add(m.id);` runs BEFORE chat_screen.dart:839 `final atBottom = _isAtBottom();` and chat_screen.dart:840 `setState(() { _messages.insert(0, m); ... })`. `_isAtBottom()` (chat_screen.dart:876-879) guards only on `_scroll.hasClients`, then reads `_scroll.position.minScrollExtent` — which in Flutter 3.44 is `double get minScrollExtent => _minScrollExtent!;` (scroll_position.dart:235) and is null until the first layout applies content dimensions. It throws. Live proof from the production error table: `select build, kind, error_type, left(stack,700) from client_errors` → build 40, platform, `_TypeError`, stack `#0 ScrollPosition.minScrollExtent (scroll_position.dart:235) / #1 _ChatScreenState._isAtBottom (features/chat/chat_screen.dart:831) / #2 _ChatScreenState._onIncoming (features/chat/chat_screen.dart:792) / #3 _ChatScreenState._subscribe.<anonymous closure> (chat_screen.dart:574) / #4 ChatRepository.subscribe.<anonymous closure> (chat_repository.dart:585)`. Still unfixed in the working tree. Flutter exposes the correct guard, `ScrollPosition.hasContentDimensions` (scroll_position.dart:240) — `grep -rn hasContentDimensions lib/` returns zero hits.
fix: Move `_ids.add(m.id)` to AFTER the successful `setState` insert so a throw cannot poison the seen-set. Independently, change `_isAtBottom()` to `if (!_scroll.hasClients || !_scroll.position.hasContentDimensions) return true;` and apply the same guard in `_scrollToNewest()` (chat_screen.dart:882-884), which reads `minScrollExtent` behind the same insufficient `hasClients` check. Add a widget test that delivers a message on the frame the ListView is first attached.

title: A failed history load tells a couple with years of messages that they have never spoken
userImpact: On any timeout, RLS hiccup, paused project or bad-network open, the chat renders the first-run empty state: "💌 Say something sweet — This is your private space, just the two of you. Send the first message." A couple three years in is told their entire history does not exist. No error, no retry button, no distinction between 'new here' and 'could not load'. That is the screenshot that ends up on Twitter.
evidence: chat_screen.dart:717-723: `try { final msgs = await ChatRepository.fetch(couple.id, warm: false); ... } catch (_) { // first-run is fine }` then chat_screen.dart:734 `setState(() => _loading = false);`. The render path at chat_screen.dart:1544 is `_messages.isEmpty ? const _EmptyChat()`, and `_EmptyChat` (chat_screen.dart:2682-2709) is the copy quoted above. There is no error state and no local message cache anywhere (`grep -rn 'messages_cache|cachedMessages|hydrate' lib/features/chat/` → no hits), so offline always means empty. Compounding it: with the fetch failed, `_maxSeq` (chat_screen.dart:431) folds over an empty list to 0, so `_catchUp` calls `ChatRepository.fetchSince(couple, 0)` — `.gt('seq', 0).order('seq', ascending: true).limit(500)` (chat_repository.dart:305-311) — which returns the couple's OLDEST 500 messages and presents them as the current conversation.
fix: Catch the fetch into a `_loadError` field instead of swallowing it. Render three distinct states: loading, loaded-and-genuinely-empty (`_EmptyChat`), and load-failed ("Couldn't reach your conversation" + Retry). Persist the last fetched page to disk (encrypted, alongside ChatDraftStore's FlutterSecureStorage pattern) so an offline open shows the real history rather than nothing. Guard `_catchUp` so it does not run with `_maxSeq == 0` after a failed initial load.
effort: 1 day for the honest states; +2 days for the local cache.

title: Push notifications can die permanently on a handset, with nothing in the app to say so or fix it
userImpact: The user stops receiving any notification — messages, calls, reaches — and the app never mentions it. For a long-distance couples app that is the product failing at its core job, and it presents to the user as "he never texts me anymore." There is no Notifications screen in Settings, so there is nothing to check and nothing to tap.
evidence: fcm_service.dart:153 `await requestPermission();` is the first statement of `registerToken()` and is unguarded; `requestPermission()` (fcm_service.dart:130-133) is a bare `await FirebaseMessaging.instance.requestPermission();`. Live production error: `client_errors` build 42, kind=platform, `FirebaseException`, received_at 2026-08-17 00:52:21, stack `#3 MethodChannelFirebaseMessaging.requestPermission (method_channel_messaging.dart:297) / #4 FcmService.requestPermission (core/services/fcm_service.dart:132) / #5 FcmService.registerToken (core/services/fcm_service.dart:153)`. When it throws, everything after it in `registerToken` is skipped: the 4-attempt `getToken()` retry loop, `_save(token)` (which writes `profiles.fcm_token`), and the `onTokenRefresh` listener registration — so no token is stored and no refresh hook exists. Both call sites discard the future (main.dart:378 `FcmService.registerToken();` on resume, app_shell.dart:185 in `_onReady`), so it surfaces only as a client_errors row. Settings has no notification-permission UI: `grep -rni notification lib/features/settings/*.dart` returns only "Pause notifications" at settings_screen.dart:784, which is the contact-pause safety feature, not the OS permission.
fix: Wrap `requestPermission()` in try/catch so a permission failure cannot abort token registration — the token fetch should still run. Add a Notifications row in Settings showing the live OS permission state (`FirebaseMessaging.instance.getNotificationSettings()`) plus whether `profiles.fcm_token` is currently non-null, with a button to `openAppSettings()`. Surface a dismissible banner on Home when pushes are off.

title: The app has no idea whether it is online: no offline banner, no auto-retry when signal returns
userImpact: On mobile data across countries — which is the entire user base — sends fail and simply sit there marked failed. When the train comes out of the tunnel nothing happens; the user must notice each failed bubble and tap retry individually. Meanwhile every screen that fails to load shows an empty state rather than "you're offline", so the app reads as broken rather than disconnected.
evidence: `grep -rn 'connectivity|Connectivity|InternetAddress.lookup|onConnectivityChanged' lib/ pubspec.yaml` → zero hits. No `connectivity_plus` (or any network-state package) in pubspec.yaml dependencies. `ChatSendQueue` (chat_send_queue.dart) imports only dart:async, dart:convert, dart:io, foundation, supabase_service, chat_broadcast_service, chat_repository, shared_preferences, uuid — it does not listen to `realtimeResumed`, even though realtime_resume.dart:32 calls the socket opening "the most literal signal this app has for 'the network came back'". `_pump()` (chat_send_queue.dart:379) is only ever invoked from enqueue, restore, manual `retry()`, and the `finally` of a completed send.
fix: Add `connectivity_plus`, expose a single `isOnline` notifier, and (a) render a persistent slim offline banner in the app shell, (b) have `ChatSendQueue` listen to both that notifier and `realtimeResumed` and call `_pump()` with backoff, flipping failed→sending automatically. This is one small file plus two listeners; it converts the app's worst-network behaviour from 'silently stuck' to 'catches up by itself'.

title: A pending or failed text message is destroyed by a process kill, silently, after the input bar has already cleared
userImpact: User types a message with no signal, presses send, the bubble shows sending, they lock the phone. Android kills the backgrounded process. The message is gone — not in the outbox, not in the input bar, not on the server — and the sender believes it was sent. They find out days later during an argument about being ignored.
evidence: chat_send_queue.dart:237-240, verbatim: "Deliberately NOT persisted across a process kill, unlike [_pending]: the bodies would sit in plain SharedPreferences... A text send is a single insert — it lands in seconds or the sender is looking at a bubble they can retry." `_text` is a plain in-memory `List<PendingText>` (chat_send_queue.dart:123); only `_pending` (media) is written to SharedPreferences by `_persist()` (chat_send_queue.dart:304-336). The premise is contradicted by the same file at chat_send_queue.dart:102-104: "Android kills this app while it is backgrounded, and backgrounding is when the disguise cover goes up — so it is the ordinary case here, not a rare one." The input bar clears on send, so the queue holds the only copy (its own comment, chat_send_queue.dart:424-425). Related silent loss: `_restore()` (chat_send_queue.dart:353) drops any persisted media send whose temp file the OS has since cleared with `continue` — the photo vanishes with no notice.
fix: Persist `_text` the same way `_pending` is, but into FlutterSecureStorage rather than SharedPreferences — ChatDraftStore already does exactly this for drafts (chat_draft_store.dart:19-21, `AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true)`), so the privacy objection in the comment is already solved elsewhere in the same feature. For dropped media restores, keep the entry and mark it failed-file-missing so the user is told.

title: Presence writes outnumber actual messages 24 to 1, and every one fans out through the realtime path Supabase documents as not scaling
userImpact: Nothing today. At 10,000 couples this is the line item that makes the app unaffordable and the backend slow — realtime latency degrades for the features that matter (message delivery, call signalling) because the same socket is saturated with 'I'm here' traffic.
evidence: `select relname, n_tup_ins, n_tup_upd from pg_stat_user_tables where relname in ('presence','messages')` → presence: 24 inserts, **83,511 updates**; messages: 3,518 inserts. That is 23.7 presence updates per message sent, from 3 accounts total. Project created 2026-06-23, so the window is at most 55 days ⇒ **≥1,518 presence updates per couple per day** (a lower bound; pg_stat has no reset timestamp). `select tablename from pg_publication_tables where pubname='supabase_realtime'` confirms `presence` is published (along with 39 other tables), so each update is a WAL event → per-subscriber RLS evaluation → delivered realtime message. Sources: main.dart:291 `Timer.periodic(const Duration(seconds: 30), (_) => beat())` calling `PresenceService.setOnline`, plus home_screen.dart:93's 15s location loop writing the same row. At 10,000 couples: ≥15M realtime messages/day ≈ 450M/month. Pro includes 5M/month then $2.50/M ⇒ roughly $1,100/month for presence alone, before storage or egress.
fix: Stop routing presence through postgres_changes. Supabase Realtime has a purpose-built Presence channel feature that is ephemeral, never touches the WAL, and never evaluates RLS per row — move `is_online`/`last_seen` onto it and keep the `presence` table only for the durable fields (location mode, screen). Separately, make the 30s heartbeat write-on-change rather than write-on-tick: it currently re-stamps an identical row 120 times an hour.
effort: 3-4 days, and it is the highest-leverage change on this list for cost.

title: The Home screen requests a fresh high-accuracy GPS fix plus four network round trips every 15 seconds, with no distance filter
userImpact: Phone gets warm and the battery visibly drops while Home is open. On a metered plan abroad — the exact situation this app is built for — it also burns data continuously for a position that has not changed. Users blame 'the app' and uninstall; some will leave a one-star review naming battery drain.
evidence: home_screen.dart:93 `_locationTimer = Timer.periodic(const Duration(seconds: 15), (_) async { ... _noteBlock(await LocationService.shareCurrent(couple.id)); await _refreshMyCoords(); })`. Each tick executes, in `LocationService.shareCurrent` → `shareOnce` (location_service.dart:79-127): `PresenceService.fetchMine(coupleId)` (DB read), `Geolocator.getCurrentPosition(LocationSettings(accuracy: LocationAccuracy.high))` for mode 'precise' (a fresh GPS fix, location_service.dart:88-92), `placemarkFromCoordinates(...)` (reverse geocode, location_service.dart:97), `PresenceService.setLocation(...)` (DB write), then home_screen.dart's `_refreshMyCoords()` adds `Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition()`. That is 240 high-accuracy fixes and ~960 network operations per hour of Home being open. There is no movement threshold anywhere — a phone on a bedside table pays exactly the same as one in a car.
fix: Replace the polling timer with `Geolocator.getPositionStream(LocationSettings(distanceFilter: 100, accuracy: LocationAccuracy.medium))` so the OS wakes you on real movement instead of every 15s. Publish on change only. Cache the reverse-geocode label keyed to ~1 km so a stationary user geocodes once, not 240 times an hour. Keep `getCurrentPosition` for the one-shot on screen entry.

title: Cold start blocks on a network call before the first Flutter frame — up to 30 seconds of frozen system splash
userImpact: On a captive-portal hotel wifi, a dead cell, or a slow 3G handshake, the user taps the icon and stares at a motionless splash screen for up to half a minute with no spinner, no text, and no way to cancel. Most people conclude the app is broken and force-close it. It also drags Play Console's cold-start vitals.
evidence: main.dart:114 `await Future.wait([TermsGate.load(), ReleaseGate.check()]);` sits between the init group and `runApp(...)` at main.dart:137 — nothing paints until it resolves. `ReleaseGate.check()` (release_gate.dart:84-100) issues `SupabaseService.client.from('app_release').select(...).limit(1).maybeSingle()` and sets no timeout of its own, so its only ceiling is `TimeoutHttpClient`'s default `timeout = Duration(seconds: 30)` (timeout_http_client.dart:18). `TermsGate.load()` (terms_gate.dart:58-66) does a local read then `await fetchAcceptedVersion()` — a second network call on the same pre-frame path.
fix: Move both off the pre-frame path. `ReleaseGate` already has a `revision` ValueNotifier that main.dart:713 rebuilds on, and `TermsGate` is consulted by a router redirect — so both can start unawaited and drive the UI when they land. If a value genuinely must be settled before the first frame, give it its own short deadline: `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 3), onTimeout: () {})` — the gate already fails open by design (release_gate.dart:81-83).

title: 23% of the arm64 install is two ML Kit models powering one optional camera flourish that mostly returns 'unknown'
userImpact: Every user downloads and permanently stores ~23 MB for a feature almost none of them will use, on top of ~20 MB for a second map SDK. On Play, install size is a measurable conversion killer in exactly the markets a long-distance app sells into — and the device storage never comes back.
evidence: Measured from E:\LDR\Miles.apk (230,159,258 bytes) with zipfile: `assets/mlkit_pose` = 12,332,190 B (15 files), `lib/arm64-v8a/libxeno_native.so` = 10,260,032 B (the subject-segmentation runtime) ⇒ 22.6 MB of an arm64 payload totalling ~97 MB (lib/arm64-v8a 70,370,048 B + mlkit_pose 12.3 MB + dex ~13.3 MB). Their only consumers are touch_map_screen.dart:368 `ReactionGestureService.detectGesture(...)` and touch_map_screen.dart:375 `ReactionSegmentService.removeBackground(...)`, both already fully optional — the first returns `ReactionGesture.unknown` on any failure (reaction_gesture_service.dart:22-27) and the second `return null` with the caller falling back to the original file (touch_map_screen.dart:376). Worse, the model is the wrong one for the job: `reaction_gesture_service.dart:31-38` reads `PoseLandmarkType.leftThumb/leftIndex/leftPinky`, which in ML Kit pose detection are single coarse points per hand, not finger joints — separating 'pinch' from 'point' from 'squeeze' from three points is not something that model can do reliably, and `if (poses.isEmpty) return unknown` means a close-up of a hand with no body in frame yields nothing at all. Separately, two full map SDKs ship: `lib/arm64-v8a/libmapbox-maps.so` 13,404,120 B + `libmapbox-common.so` 6,890,256 B = 20.3 MB for world_map_screen.dart (reached only by a tap at partner_location_card.dart:301), while `google_maps_flutter` independently serves location_map_screen.dart.
fix: Drop `google_mlkit_pose_detection` and `google_mlkit_subject_segmentation` entirely and delete the two services — the feature already degrades to exactly the no-ML behaviour, so removal is a deletion, not a rewrite (~23 MB). If the background cut-out is worth keeping, use ML Kit's Play-services-delivered (unbundled) Selfie Segmentation so the model downloads on demand rather than shipping. Then pick ONE map SDK: Mapbox alone can serve both screens (~another 0 MB saved but Google Play Services Maps dex drops out), or Google Maps alone saves the full 20.3 MB and loses only the 3D terrain screen. Both cuts together take arm64 from ~97 MB to ~54 MB. Also confirm you are shipping an AAB — the 219 MB figure is the universal APK carrying x86_64 (78.8 MB) and armeabi-v7a (53.0 MB) that Play would never deliver to a real phone.
effort: ML Kit removal: half a day. Map consolidation: 1-2 days.

title: A realtime subscription that fails to join five times gives up forever, and the only signal it emits goes to a function that does nothing
userImpact: The screen silently stops updating. Messages, presence, receipts, the rewrap ceremony — whichever channel died just never delivers again, and it looks identical to a partner who has gone quiet. Nobody, including the developer, ever learns it happened.
